defects.location: test_parseport.py test_rejects_port_above_max / test_rejects_very_large_port — both tests exercise the same single code path (port > 65535); '999999' adds no distinct branch coverage over '65536' and reads as padding rather than intent-revealing testing
defects.fix: Drop test_rejects_very_large_port, or keep it only if it is meant to guard a hypothetical overflow path and say so in the test name; one above-max case plus the boundary test at 65535 is sufficient for this one-line range check

defects.location: parseport.py — the range literal 65535 appears twice (comparison and f-string message) and the bound is duplicated again in the tests; trivial here, but a module-level MAX_PORT = 65535 constant would keep the message and the check from drifting apart if the range ever changes
defects.fix: Optional: introduce MAX_PORT = 65535 (and MIN_PORT = 1) and reference it in both the check and the error message; equally acceptable to leave as-is for a module this size — not a blocking issue
